title: Observability fair-queueing and backpressure for VPC collectors
creator: Marcus Lee
description:
Problem: In Dedicated/VPC and on-prem deployments we observe noisy-tenant effects where a small number of high-throughput tenants cause increased tail latency, queueing blow-ups, and uneven resource consumption in collector ingestion pipelines. This ticket implements a defend-in-depth approach: per-tenant fair-queueing (approximate SFQ/H-TBF), coordinated backpressure signals to upstream SDKs/proxies, and observability surfaces (metrics + dashboards + alerts) to measure fairness and to detect tenant quarantining events.

Goals: (1) enforce tenant fairness across ingestion workers so a single tenant cannot saturate collector CPU / network buffers, (2) surface clear metrics and SLOs for per-tenant latency and ingestion drop rates, (3) provide an automated quarantine and rate-down mechanism when a tenant exceeds configurable thresholds, with safe defaults for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private modes, (4) expose backpressure signals upstream via headers and SDK hooks so customers can adapt batching/emit behavior.

Scope: changes live in the perimeter collector binary (rust service), the reverse-proxy plugin used in VPC connectors, SDK header convention (X-Redwood-Backpressure: level=notice|throttle|quarantine), Console dashboards and alert rules, and a canary rollout plan.

Success criteria: new collectors in staging maintain 99th-percentile ingest latency <200ms under mixed-tenant synthetic load, noisy tenant throttled to configured share without causing global tail latency regressions, console shows per-tenant "fair_share_utilization" metric with sandbox dashboards, and a documented rollback plan and tenant-impacting customer communication template.
acceptance_criteria: Collector implements per-tenant queueing and enforces configurable max-shares per tenant
Backpressure header emitted when collector queue depth crosses thresholds and respected by reverse-proxy
Canary rollout deployed to staging and 5% of production tenants with feature flag
Dashboards: per-tenant ingest_latency_p99, fair_share_utilization, tenant_drop_rate and an alert when any tenant_drop_rate > 0.5% for 5m
Automated quarantine action documented and reversible via Console for support teams
comments: 2025-02-11 - Marcus Lee: Initial spike completed. Evaluated SFQ and hierarchical token bucket (H-TBF). H-TBF preferred for bursty SDK patterns because it allows reserve bursts per tenant while bounding long-term share.

2025-02-13 - Aisha Tan: Implemented a prototype bounded-channel approach in rust collector. Observed backpressure propagation via a short header spike in synthetic tests; need to standardize header format for SDK teams.

2025-02-14 - PM (Lena Ortiz): Confirmed product constraints: in Dedicated we must provide tenant isolation defaults but keep opt-out for tenants with contractual higher-throughput. Add per-tenant quota overrides as admin action in Console.

2025-02-17 - SRE (David Park): Load test results attached in Confluence. With H-TBF and per-worker sharding fairness improved: noisy tenant fair_share_utilization dropped from 0.86 to 0.32, global p99 ingest latency reduced by 45ms. Noted increased CPU due to additional queueing logic; need optimized sampling and JIT allocation.

2025-02-19 - Design (Ivy Chen): Dashboard drafts reviewed. Recommend a single pane combining per-tenant heatmap + timeline of quarantine events to simplify support triage. Will hand off widgets to Console team.
2025-02-21 - Security (Nikhil Rao): Required K8s PSP and audit log entries when quarantine actions are taken. Marked this ticket as needing formal security review (added security_review_required).

2025-02-22 - Aisha Tan: Implemented header X-Redwood-Backpressure with values {level=notice, reason=queue_depth, suggested_hold_ms=120}. SDK eng noted compatibility concerns; added SDK compatibility shim plan in PR description.

2025-02-24 - Marcus Lee: Canary rollout plan approved. Staged feature flag in staging, will enable 5% production tenants next week. Monitor metrics and instantiate incident runbook if false positives spike.

2025-02-25 - Aisha Tan: Open items: (1) reduce CPU overhead via adaptive sampling, (2) Console UI for manual tenant unquarantine, (3) add automated regression test in perf harness. Scheduled follow-up tickets ENG-99457..59.
